tasks.title: Build a Complete HTML5 Personal Website
tasks.description:
## Part 1 – HTML Fundamentals

Create a complete personal webpage that demonstrates the fundamental HTML elements and concepts covered in this section.

### Document Structure
- Create a valid HTML5 document using `<!DOCTYPE html>`.
- Use `<html>`, `<head>`, `<title>`, and `<body>` correctly.
- Set the page title to your name.

### Headings & Paragraphs
- Create headings from `<h1>` to `<h6>`.
- Add at least 3 paragraphs describing yourself, your education, and your hobbies.

### Text Formatting
Use the following text formatting elements at least once:
- `<b>`
- `<strong>`
- `<i>`
- `<em>`
- `<u>`
- `<mark>`
- `<small>`
- `<sub>` and `<sup>`

### Links
- Create links to Google and YouTube.
- Create a link to at least one other website.
- Make at least one link open in a new tab.
- Create an email link using `mailto:`.

### Images
- Add at least 3 images to the page.
- Give every image a meaningful `alt` attribute.
- Control image dimensions using HTML `width` and `height` attributes.

### Lists
- Create an unordered list containing your favorite foods.
- Create an ordered list containing your daily routine.
- Create a nested list containing categories and sub-items.
- Create a description list using `<dl>`, `<dt>`, and `<dd>`.

### Tables
Create a student grades table that includes:
- A `<caption>` describing the table.
- A header row using `<th>` elements.
- At least 5 students.
- At least 4 subjects.
- Proper use of `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, and `<td>`.

### Forms
Create a registration form containing:
- Text input.
- Email input.
- Password input.
- Number input.
- Date input.
- Radio buttons.
- Checkboxes.
- Select menu.
- Textarea.
- Submit button.

Use a corresponding `<label>` for every form control and use appropriate input types and `required` attributes where suitable.
tasks.hint: Build the page section by section. Start with the HTML5 document structure, then add headings and text, followed by links, images, lists, the grades table, and finally the registration form. Focus on using the correct HTML element for each type of content rather than relying on `<div>` elements.

tasks.title: Build a Semantic Academy Website
tasks.description:
## Part 2 – Semantic HTML Elements

Build a complete webpage for a fictional academy using semantic HTML elements instead of creating the entire layout with generic `<div>` elements.

### Page Structure
Use the following semantic elements appropriately:
- `<header>` – Page or section header.
- `<nav>` – Navigation links.
- `<main>` – Main page content.
- `<section>` – Thematic sections of content.
- `<article>` – Independent content such as a course article.
- `<aside>` – Related or secondary information.
- `<footer>` – Footer information.

### Academy Content
The fictional academy website must contain:
- A header containing the academy name.
- A navigation menu with relevant links.
- A main content area containing an introduction to the academy.
- At least two sections presenting different courses.
- An article describing one of the courses in more detail.
- An aside containing contact information or other useful information.

### Media
- Add a `<figure>` containing an academy-related image.
- Add a `<figcaption>` describing the image.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- Create an FAQ area using `<details>` and `<summary>`.
- Include multiple questions and expandable answers.

### Footer
- Add a footer containing copyright information and any other relevant footer content.

The final webpage should have a clear semantic structure where each element represents the purpose of its content.
tasks.hint: Think about the meaning of each section before choosing an element. Use `<header>` and `<nav>` for the top of the page, `<main>` for the primary content, `<section>` for groups of related content, `<article>` for the detailed course content, `<aside>` for secondary information, and `<footer>` for the bottom of the page. Use `<details>` and `<summary>` to create expandable FAQ items.

tasks.title: Build a Complete HTML & CSS Website
tasks.description:
## Part 1 – HTML & CSS

Create a complete personal webpage that demonstrates the HTML elements and CSS properties covered in this section.

### Document Structure
- Create a valid HTML5 document using `<!DOCTYPE html>`.
- Use `<html>`, `<head>`, `<title>`, and `<body>` correctly.
- Set the page title to your name.
- Use CSS to set a suitable page background color, font family, and text color.

### Headings & Paragraphs
- Create headings from `<h1>` to `<h6>`.
- Add at least 3 paragraphs describing yourself, your education, and your hobbies.
- Use CSS to style the headings with different font sizes, colors, and spacing.
- Add suitable spacing between paragraphs.

### Text Formatting
Use the following text formatting elements at least once:
- `<b>`
- `<strong>`
- `<i>`
- `<em>`
- `<u>`
- `<mark>`
- `<small>`
- `<sub>` and `<sup>`

Use CSS to change the font style and color of some formatted text and add suitable spacing where needed.

### Links
- Create links to Google and YouTube.
- Create a link to at least one other website.
- Make at least one link open in a new tab.
- Create an email link using `mailto:`.
- Use CSS to change the links' color and font size and add suitable spacing around them.

### Images
- Add at least 3 images to the page.
- Give every image a meaningful `alt` attribute.
- Control image width and height using HTML attributes.
- Use CSS to add borders around the images.
- Use margin and padding to create suitable spacing around the images.

### Lists
- Create an unordered list containing your favorite foods.
- Create an ordered list containing your daily routine.
- Create a nested list containing categories and sub-items.
- Create a description list using `<dl>`, `<dt>`, and `<dd>`.
- Use CSS to style list headings with suitable fonts and colors.
- Add suitable spacing between lists and their items.

### Student Grades Table
Create a student grades table that includes:
- A `<caption>` describing the table.
- A header row using `<th>` elements.
- At least 5 students.
- At least 4 subjects.
- Proper use of `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, and `<td>`.

Use CSS to:
- Add borders to the table and its cells.
- Change the background and text colors of the header row.
- Add padding inside the table cells.

### Registration Form
Create a registration form containing:
- Text input.
- Email input.
- Password input.
- Number input.
- Date input.
- Radio buttons.
- Checkboxes.
- Select menu.
- Textarea.
- Submit button.

Use a corresponding `<label>` for every form control and use appropriate input types and `required` attributes where suitable.

Use CSS to:
- Add a background color, border, padding, and margin to the form.
- Style the labels, inputs, and submit button using suitable colors and fonts.

### Final Requirement
The completed webpage should be visually organized and demonstrate the HTML elements and CSS properties covered in this task, including `color`, `font`, `background`, `border`, `margin`, and `padding`.
tasks.hint: Build the HTML structure first and then style each group of elements with CSS. Keep your CSS organized by element or section so you can easily see how each property affects the page. Focus on using the required HTML elements and CSS properties rather than trying to make the page overly complex.

tasks.title: Build a Styled Semantic Academy Website
tasks.description:
## Part 2 – Semantic HTML & CSS

Build a complete and visually organized website for a fictional academy using semantic HTML elements instead of relying only on `<div>` elements. Apply CSS styling throughout the page using the properties learned in class.

### Header
Create a `<header>` containing the academy name.

Use CSS to give the header:
- A suitable background color.
- A suitable text color.
- An appropriate font.
- Padding and spacing.
- A border.

Style the academy name with a large font size, suitable color, and spacing.

### Navigation
Create a `<nav>` containing navigation links.

Use CSS to style the navigation menu with:
- A suitable background.
- Text colors.
- Borders.
- Appropriate fonts and spacing.

### Main Content
Create a `<main>` containing the primary academy content.

Use CSS to add a suitable background color, margin, and padding to the main content.

### Introduction
Add an introduction describing the fictional academy.

Use CSS to style the introduction with:
- A suitable background.
- A border.
- Padding and margin.
- An appropriate font.
- A suitable text color.

### Course Sections
Create at least two `<section>` elements representing different academy courses.

Use CSS to style each course section with:
- A border.
- A background color.
- Padding and margin.
- Suitable fonts and text colors.

### Course Article
Create an `<article>` describing one of the academy courses in more detail.

Use CSS to style the article with suitable:
- Colors.
- Fonts.
- Borders.
- Spacing.
- Background.

### Aside
Create an `<aside>` containing contact information or other useful academy information.

Use CSS to:
- Give the aside a different background color.
- Add a border.
- Use the `position` property to place the aside appropriately on the page.

### Figure & Caption
Create a `<figure>` containing an academy-related image and a `<figcaption>` describing it.

Use CSS to:
- Add borders around the figure and image.
- Add suitable spacing.
- Style the caption with an appropriate font and color.

### Frequently Asked Questions
Create an FAQ area using `<details>` and `<summary>`.

Use CSS to add:
- A border.
- A background color.
- Padding.
- Suitable margins and spacing.

### Footer
Create a `<footer>` containing copyright information.

Use CSS to give the footer:
- A different background color.
- A suitable text color.
- An appropriate font.
- Padding and spacing.
- A border.

### Final Requirement
The final result should be a complete, attractive, and visually organized academy website. Use semantic HTML elements correctly and demonstrate the CSS properties learned in class, including `color`, `font`, `background`, `border`, `margin`, `padding`, and `position`.
tasks.hint: Start by creating the semantic page structure with `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, `<figure>`, and `<footer>`. Then add the required academy content. Finally, style each semantic element with CSS. Use `position` specifically for the aside and keep the visual design consistent across the entire page.

tasks.title: Build a Modern Landing Page
tasks.description:
Create a modern landing page using HTML and CSS. Choose any idea you like, such as a restaurant, gym, product, company, academy, portfolio, or another concept of your choice.

### Navbar
- Create a navigation bar containing a logo or name.
- Add navigation links.

### Hero Section
Create a hero section containing:
- A main heading.
- A short description.
- A call-to-action button.
- A suitable image or background.

### Page Sections
- Add at least 3 different sections to the page.
- You may choose sections such as About, Services, Features, Portfolio, or Testimonials.

### Services / Features
- Create a Services or Features section.
- Include at least 3 cards.

### Contact
- Add a Contact section.
- Include a simple contact form.

### Footer
- Add a footer containing useful information or links.

### Semantic HTML
- Use semantic HTML elements where appropriate.

### CSS Design
Use CSS to create a clean and attractive design. Your design should include:
- Colors.
- Fonts.
- Spacing.
- Borders.
- Shadows.
- Hover effects.

### Layout
- Use Flexbox or CSS Grid to organize the page layout.

### Bootstrap
- You may use Bootstrap if you want.
- If you use Bootstrap, you must also write your own CSS.

### Code Quality
- Keep the HTML and CSS clean, organized, and easy to understand.

### Important
- Choose your own idea and design.
- Do not copy a complete template.
- Try to build the page by yourself.
- Focus on understanding what you write rather than just making the page work.
- Be creative. There is no single correct design.
tasks.hint: Choose a simple idea first and sketch the page structure before coding. Build the semantic HTML sections, then use Flexbox or Grid to arrange the content. After the layout works, add your colors, typography, spacing, shadows, borders, and hover effects. Keep the design simple enough that you understand every part of the code.
